newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds tighten, led by new issue fever.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds tighten, led by new issue fever.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds tightened one to two basis points across the board on Thursday in the face of faltering U.S. Treasuries, led by brisk demand for another spate of fresh supply, dealers said.
High-yield new issues also gleamed in their market, with deals upped in size to match subscriptions.

Mary Rooney, a corporate bond strategist at J.P. Morgan Securities Inc, said the increased new issue volume falls short of posing any threats to positive technical factors in the investment grade market. Industrial sector issuance is especially welcome, she said.
"Spreads are tight, fundamentals are real strong and September was a pretty light month," she said, adding that the upcoming earnings season may have more impact on underlying corporate tone.
Still, Rooney also said she foresees little in the way of earnings that could upset the positive environment.

Investment grade issuance on Thursday was topped by $400 million in A3/A debt from Union Pacific Resources via a Smith Barney Inc group. The deal included $200 million 10-year notes priced as 7s to yield 49 basis points over Treasuries and $200 million 30-year debentures priced at 65 basis points over.

New banking issuance featured $300 million in 10-year senior subordinated non-callable A1/single-A notes from First Union National Bank. The notes were priced via lead manager Salomon Brothers as 7-1/8s to yield 7.175 percent or 59 basis points over the Treasury curve.
Both tranches were said to tighten by one to two basis points in spread in the secondary.

Allegiance Corp's $550 million three-tranche Baa3/BBB-minus issue tightened by one to two basis points on Thursday, one trader said. The deal came on Wednesday with a top yield spread of 98 basis points for 20-year debentures.
Elsewhere on Thursday, NGC Corp issued $175 million 30-year Baa1/BBB-plus debentures as 7-5/8s to yield 7.666 percent or 78 basis points over the old Treasury long bond.
In the global market, Malaysia's Petroliam Nasional (Petronas) priced three A1/A-plus bonds totaling $1.9 billion through co-leads CS First Boston Corp and Salomon Brothers.

The deal was comprised of $600 million debt due 2001 priced as 6-5/8s to yield 38 basis points over Treasuries; $800 million debt due 2006 priced as 7-1/8s to yield 57 basis points over Treasuries; and $500 million debt due 2026 priced as 7-5/8s to yield 84 basis points over Treasuries.
The deal was oversubscribed, sources said.

Turning to high-yielders, fiery demand was confirmed by the successful pricings of deals from Paging Network Inc and U.S. Can Corp, traders said. The deals were increased in size by $150 million and $50 million, repectively, and proceeded to garner higher aftermarket prices.

Paging Network's $500 million rule 144A senior subordinated notes of 2008 were priced at par to yield 10.0 percent via Goldman Sachs & Co and Salomon Brothers Inc. The notes were quoted at 100-1/2 bid Thursday afternoon.
U.S. Can's $275 million rule 144A 10-year senior subordinated notes were priced at par to yield 10.125 percent. The notes were quoted up to 101-1/4-101-1/2 in thin afternoon trade, a dealer said.
Both issues were rated B2/single-B.

In the U.S. Treasury market, prices slipped early after the Labor Department said first time jobless claims fell 22,000 in the week ended October 5 to a seasonally adjusted 319,000. Analysts expected claims would rise modestly.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond closed down 22/32 at 98-9/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
